Ally Logistic, CapitaLand Investment break ground on Omega 1 Singapore along Gul Lane
article:
Taiwan’s largest logistics infrastructure developer Ally Logistic Property (ALP) and Singapore-listed real asset manager CapitaLand Investment (CLI) have broken ground on Omega 1 Singapore, a five-storey smart logistics facility in Tuas.

Located at 19 Gul Lane and targeted for completion in the second half of 2028, the $260 million development is an asset under CLI’s CapitaLand Southeast Asia Logistics Fund.

This is also the first time ALP is deploying its integrated Omega logistics infrastructure platform in Singapore.

The platform, developed and proven in Taiwan, aims to help businesses improve fulfilment speed, operational visibility and supply chain resilience. It combines industrial real estate, shared automation, proprietary software and AI-enabled operational tools.

“As supply chains are restructured, labour becomes scarcer and AI reshapes operations, businesses need infrastructure that connects physical assets, automation, software and intelligence as one system,” said Charlie Chang, CEO and co-founder of ALP.

With the Omega platform, businesses can scale their operations more efficiently without having to bear significant upfront costs to develop separate infrastructure and integrate multiple systems, according to a Sept 24 joint release by ALP and CLI.

This supports higher logistics throughput, reduces reliance on labour-intensive processes and allows businesses to expand more flexibly in line with demand, the release added.

“Demand from institutional investors and occupiers for technology-enabled logistics infrastructure continues to grow across Asia Pacific," said Patricia Goh, CEO, Southeast Asia, and global head of logistics and self-storage at CLI.

The Omega 1 Singapore development will be situated within the western industrial and logistics cluster.

As it is near Tuas Port, Tuas Checkpoint and Jurong Port, it will support domestic distribution, regional fulfilment and cross-border logistics flows.

JTC chief executive Jacqueline Poh noted that optimising land use and adopting technology at scale will be critical to Singapore’s next phase of logistics growth.

“Omega 1 Singapore demonstrates how innovative infrastructure partnerships can support a more competitive and future-ready logistics ecosystem, reinforcing Singapore’s role as a leading global trade and logistics hub,” Poh added.

This January, CLI had announced that it will develop Omega 1 Singapore , its first smart logistics facility, as part of its next phase of logistics growth across Asia Pacific.

That came alongside CLI’s acquisition of a minority stake in ALP, which is also an existing capital partner in the CapitaLand Southeast Asia Logistics Fund.

When completed, the Singapore facility will have a gross floor area of 764,244 sq ft, with a storage capacity of 60,000 pallet positions.

It is expected to be fully leased to ALP under a long-term master lease with built-in rent escalation, providing the investors in the CLI fund with stable and growing income, according to the Jan 8 release.

Elsewhere in Southeast Asia, ALP has Omega facilities already operating or under development in Malaysia and Thailand.

Under the CapitaLand Southeast Asia Logistics Fund, the Omega 1 Bang Na built-to-suit smart logistics campus is being developed in the Greater Bangkok Metropolitan Area.

That will be Thailand’s biggest standalone logistics campus, with the first phase to be completed by end-September 2026.

title: Five-room flat at Pinnacle@Duxton sets record of $1.72mil; Kallang-Whampoa five-room flat sets town record of $1.59 mil
article:
Two record-setting five-room HDB flat resale transactions took place recently, one at The Pinnacle@Duxton and another along Upper Boon Keng Road.

Five-room flat at Pinnacle@Duxton changed hands at $1.72 million, setting a fresh record for HDB flats in Central Area

A five-room flat at 1C Cantonment Road , part of The Pinnacle@Duxton, was sold for $1.72 million ($1,494 psf) in September 2026. This is the highest price recorded for a five-room HDB resale flat at the development and in the Central Area HDB town. The transaction also set the highest psf record for HDB resale flat in the Central Area HDB town.

Located on the 19th to 21st storeys, the flat measures 1,151 sq ft. It has a remaining lease of approximately 84 years, with the lease commencing in 2011.

This transaction surpasses the previous high of $1.701 million ($1,477 psf) for a five-room flat at the development, located on a higher floor. That record was set just over two weeks earlier, on Sept 9 this year, at 1B Cantonment Road (see Table 1). The earlier sale was on the 28th to 30th storeys, about nine storeys above the subject flat. Largely unrenovated, it was first purchased about two decades ago as a first home , EdgeProp Singapore reported.

All 10 of the highest-priced HDB resale transactions in the Central Area HDB town were for five-room flats at The Pinnacle@Duxton. Each of the development’s seven blocks, 1A to 1G Cantonment Road, has 88 five-room flats and 176 four-room flats.

Islandwide, 11 HDB resale flats have transacted for $1.6 million or more so far in 2026, compared with five in the whole of 2025. Three of this year's 11 were at The Pinnacle@Duxton.

The high price fetched by the subject flat could be attributed to it being part of The Pinnacle@Duxton, regarded as one of Singapore’s iconic HDB developments. Its city-fringe location, distinctive design and CBD proximity may have also contributed. The flat's relatively long remaining lease may have further supported the price.

The flat is a short walk from Maxwell, Tanjong Pagar and Outram Park MRT stations, which offer access to the Thomson-East Coast, East-West and North East lines (see Map 1).

Nearby retail options include 100AM, Tanjong Pagar Plaza , Icon Village and Chinatown Point . Cantonment Primary School and Outram Secondary School are within a 2km radius.

The subject flat transacted below the current HDB resale record of $1.728 (see Table 2). That said, it commands the highest psf among the top five resale transactions at $1,494.

Table 2 does not include a five-room flat at Skyoasis @ Dawson in Queenstown, reported by EdgeProp Singapore in July 2024 as sold for $1.726 million . That price would place it ahead of the subject flat, though the transaction does not appear in the current HDB dataset.

Five-room flat in Upper Boon Keng Road sets a new record of $1.59 mil for flats of its type in Kallang-Whampoa town

Meanwhile, a five-room flat at 8A Upper Boon Keng Road changed hands for $1.59 million ($1,273 psf) in September 2026. The 1,248 sq ft flat is located on the 28th to 30th storeys and has a remaining lease of about 89 years.

This transaction surpassed the previous high of $1.55 million ($1,231 psf) for five-room flats in Kallang-Whampoa recorded in October 2025 (see Table 3). That flat was on the 31st to 33rd storeys at 8 Boon Keng Road, part of City View @ Boon Keng, a Design, Build and Sell Scheme project.

The subject flat is part of Kallang Trivista , which has three blocks comprising 808 units. These include studio apartments as well as two-, three-, four- and five-room flats.

Next to the development is Kallang Horizon, a 477-unit Build-To-Order (BTO) project launched as part of the November 2022 BTO sales exercise . Across the river lies the Kallang Close government land sale site , which was awarded to a joint venture between Frasers Property and Mitsubishi Estate in April 2026.

In terms of public transport connectivity, the subject flat is within a five-minute walk to Kallang MRT Station which serves the East-West Line and provides access to the city centre (see Map 2). It is also near Lorong 1 Geylang Bus Terminal. Bendemeer MRT Station on the Downtown Line is a longer, 15-minute walk away.

Amenities in the vicinity include Upper Boon Keng Market and Food Centre, as well as supermarkets such as FairPrice and Sheng Siong. A wider range of retail options is available further away at Bugis Junction and Kallang Wave Mall.

Schools such as Bendemeer Primary School, Geylang Methodist School (Primary), Hong Wen School, Geylang Methodist School (Secondary), Bendemeer Secondary School and Northlight School are located within a 2km radius.

Looking ahead, the wider Kallang area is set to benefit from URA's Kallang Alive masterplan. Under the masterplan, the area around the Singapore Sports Hub will be redeveloped into a car-lite, waterfront destination, with new public spaces and recreational facilities.

Closer to the subject flat, Kallang MRT Station is slated to be integrated with a new bus interchange under the upcoming Kallang Horizon public housing project. The interchange is expected to replace the existing Lorong 1 Geylang Bus Terminal.

title: Far East Orchard to acquire London site for $102 mil, plans 444-bed student housing development
article:
Far East Orchard is acquiring a freehold development site at 325 Borough High Street in Southwark, London, for GBP60 million ($102 million), with plans to develop a 444-bed purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA) project.

Known as King’s Place, the site is located in Central London’s Zone 1. The proposed development will also include a separate eight-unit key worker accommodation block, Far East Orchard announced on Sept 24.

Planning permission for the development was granted by Southwark Council in February 2024, while Gateway 2 approval was obtained in July 2026. The latter is a key regulatory milestone that allows construction to commence.

The development is targeted for completion in 2029, ahead of the 2029/30 academic year. It will feature communal lounges, health and wellness facilities and outdoor spaces, and is targeting a BREEAM Outstanding sustainability rating.

King’s Place is about a seven-minute walk from King’s College London and is also near the London School of Economics and Political Science, Queen Mary University of London and Imperial College London.

The site is a four-minute walk from Borough Underground station and an eight-minute walk from Elephant & Castle station. Supermarkets, a post office and other amenities are also within walking distance.

Far East Orchard says London’s student accommodation market continues to face a structural supply imbalance, supported by a large domestic and international student population and constraints on new development.

King’s Place will be Far East Orchard’s first development in London and the third acquisition under the FE UK Student Accommodation Development Fund (FESAD), its UK PBSA development fund.

The acquisition will bring FESAD’s development portfolio to 956 PBSA beds across London, Manchester and Glasgow.

The fund’s other developments comprise a 273-bed project on Osborne Street in Glasgow, which topped out in April and is expected to be completed in 2027, and a 239-bed development at Plymouth Grove in Manchester. The latter received Gateway 2 approval in July and has commenced construction, with completion slated for 2028.

Upon completion, King’s Place is expected to be managed by Homes for Students, a subsidiary of Far East Orchard.

Alan Tang, group CEO of Far East Orchard, says London remains one of the UK’s most attractive and supply-constrained student accommodation markets. He adds that King’s Place expands the group’s development portfolio across three major UK cities.

The acquisition is being undertaken through Borough High Street Development, a joint venture company in which FESAD holds an 85% stake. Far East Orchard Investments (UK) and Aurum Investments, a subsidiary of Woh Hup Holdings, each hold 7.5%.

The acquisition is expected to be completed within three weeks of the sale and purchase agreement dated Sept 24, or earlier if agreed by the buyer and seller.

title: How Andrea De Cruz’s liver transplant changed the way she cooks at home — using V-ZUG
article:
For Andrea De Cruz, food has been closely tied to some of the biggest changes in her life.

In 2002, the podcaster and entrepreneur underwent a liver transplant, with her then-boyfriend and now husband, Mediacorp actor Pierre Png, donating part of his liver. More than two decades later, the experience continues to shape how she takes care of her health, particularly the way she eats.

“Since the transplant, I’ve taken quite good care of my meals,” says the 52-year-old. “I hardly ever eat fried food. We like to steam food and eat clean.”

At home, that translates into relatively simple meals.

De Cruz prefers drawing flavour from the ingredients themselves — soup, for instance, might be prepared with scallops, red dates and wolfberries instead of chicken stock, while mushrooms are another ingredient she uses to add flavour.

She and Png eat at home around five evenings a week, making ease and convenience important considerations in the kitchen. “These days, I tend to look for simpler recipes and appliances that make cooking easier,” she says.

Those considerations became particularly relevant when the couple decided to renovate a penthouse in the east that they have owned for 16 years.

Choosing V-ZUG for their revamped kitchen

After renting out the property for several years, the couple took the opportunity to refresh the apartment in 2024 when they decided to move back in. The idea was to make the penthouse their own again and create a home where they could entertain friends.

In the kitchen, she wanted appliances that suited the way she cooks.

By then, De Cruz was already familiar with V-ZUG, having used the Swiss household appliance brand in the couple’s other home, and decided to return to it when fitting out the home.

She eventually opted for a suite of V-ZUG appliances comprising the Combi-Steam 60cm oven (MSLQ), CombiCooler V4000, Adora dishwasher and CombiCookTop V4000 . The home is also equipped with the Adora range washing machine and dryer .

“I love V-ZUG for their efficiency and how well they operate,” she says.

One of De Cruz’s favourite V-ZUG appliances is the Combi-Steam 60cm oven , which combines microwave, oven and steaming functions within a single unit. Having these functions in a single appliance also saves space, reducing the need for separate appliances that would otherwise take up room in the kitchen.

“For an apartment with much smaller space, you don’t need three different appliances, so this one works well for us,” she says.

The V-ZUG CombiCookTop V4000 , on the other hand, is installed on a movable island. Its integrated extraction system removes the need for a conventional hood suspended above the cooking area, leaving the space above the island open.

While the kitchen is equipped for different ways of cooking, De Cruz tends to return to the methods that suit her everyday meals, particularly braising, steaming and grilling.

Keeping things simple with steaming

Steaming is one of the functions De Cruz uses most frequently, particularly for fish and vegetables. With the V-ZUG’s Combi-Steam 60cm oven , she can set the food to cook and go about her day, rather than continuously monitoring the cooking process.

“It gives me more flexibility in the kitchen, so I can get other things done at the same time,” she says.

Having previously tried appliances from other brands, she notes she has encountered models where one mode worked better than another. Her experience with V-ZUG has been different.

“Each function works as good as the other without compromise,” she shares, adding being able to prepare different parts of a meal in the same appliance also means less to clean afterwards. “There’s very little to clean up after, unlike if you were to use the conventional stove.”

Her time in the kitchen also extends beyond cooking for herself and Png. She also sets aside time every few days to meal prep for another member of the household: their five-year-old frenchie, Bruno.

Cooking with Bruno in mind

Highly food-motivated and inquisitive, Bruno is rarely far away when De Cruz is preparing food.

“He’s such a rambunctious boy,” she chuckles. “He’s always checking back to see how you are. He’s also very curious and wants to poke his nose into everything.”

The couple adopted Bruno during the COVID-19 period, drawn to his sweet nature and lively personality. “He runs around and does all his zoomies,” she says.

Due to his extremely active nature, Bruno suffered a spinal injury and was subsequently found to have a degenerative bone condition. Additionally, having previously raised three Shih Tzus, De Cruz admits that watching her late dogs’ needs change as they grew older made her more conscious of how she takes care of Bruno.

His diet is now something she pays close attention to, particularly his intake of omega-rich food.

De Cruz would prepare several days’ worth of food for Bruno in advance, using the same V-ZUG appliances she relies on for her own cooking.

“Having an appliance that can serve so many different purposes makes things much easier for me,” she says. “As a wife and mother to a furkid, I feel like I’m doing my best. Being able to experiment with new food and healthy recipes gives me purpose.”

title: Crypto exchange Bitget says hackers stole US$352 mil
article:
(Sept 25): Crypto exchange Bitget reported an estimated US$351.6 million in unauthorised transfers from some of its wallets and temporarily suspended withdrawals.

“User funds are safe,” chief executive Gracy Chen said in a post on X early Friday in Singapore. “The full amount of this loss falls within the coverage of Bitget’s User Protection Fund, which currently holds over US$464 million.”

[SECURITY NOTICE] Bitget Hot Wallet Incident — September 24, 2026

At 18:31 UTC on September 24, 2026, Bitget's security systems detected unauthorized transfers from some of our hot wallets. Our security team activated emergency response protocols immediately.

What we have…— Gracy Chen @Bitget (@GracyBitget) September 24, 2026

The hack continues a spate of recent attacks that have put crypto cybersecurity in the spotlight. Earlier this month, US$320 million worth of Bitcoin was drained from a wallet used by Liquid Network, while in August the hack of the popular offline Bitcoin wallet Coldcard raised questions about the safest way to store the digital asset.

Founded in 2018, Bitget is one of the leading centralised crypto exchanges globally. It was among those that grew rapidly after the collapse of FTX in 2022 as traders shifted activity to surviving platforms. The Seychelles-registered exchange currently has 120 million registered users, according to its website.

The hack “is one of the most substantive centralised exchange exploits of 2026” and “another wake-up call for the digital-assets industry,” said Esme Pau, head of capital markets and policy at blockchain security firm CertiK. “The scale of the drain at around three quarters of the exchange’s User Protection Fund transcends a security lapse and makes it a crisis event.”

See also: Bitcoin bulls eye next leg as US$15 bil options expiry nears

The hackers swapped about US$183 million of the stolen funds for Ether tokens, according to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain.

See also: Bitcoin ETF flows turn positive after US$4.6 bil rebound

Chen said Bitget operates a three-tier wallet architecture and the breach was confined to portions of hot-wallet and warm-wallet layers, with cold wallets remaining secure. Hot wallets stay online for frequent transactions, cold wallets stay offline for maximum security, while warm wallets sit in between.

“Deposits and trading remain fully operational,” Chen said. “Withdrawals are temporarily paused and will be restored as soon as the security review is complete.”

A full incident report including root cause analysis and corrective actions will be published within 24 hours, she said.

In preliminary comments on the method of the hack, Chen said on X that hackers had “compromised a critical backend system” and “used it to spoof transaction data.” The company suspects North Korea, she said in a livestream on X.

In a separate post, Chen said that stolen assets include Ether, XRP, BNB, AVAX, USDT and USDC, adding that some of the foundations of the affected chains are freezing the hackers’ wallet addresses to prevent the funds from being swapped out.

Aneirin Flynn, chief executive of cybersecurity technology firm FailSafe, said the significance of the Bitget hack “is that it destroys the illusion that major exchanges have solved hot-wallet security.”

“Even though their protection fund covers the loss, a breach of this size severely damages institutional trust in crypto infrastructure,” he said.

title: Suzuki eyes making cars twice as fast to keep up with China
article:
(Sept 25): Suzuki Motor Corp aims to develop cars twice as fast to maintain its competitive edge in an industry reshaped by Chinese automakers.

The Japanese manufacturer eyes slashing vehicle development times to 24 months by the end of this decade, from the 40 to 48 months it takes now, chief executive officer Toshihiro Suzuki said Friday.

“Chinese manufacturers have incredible speed,” Suzuki told reporters in Tokyo. “To keep up, we need to figure out how to move faster.”

After decades of measuring themselves against Japanese efficiency or German engineering, car executives are looking to China’s automakers as a new benchmark. The likes of BYD, Leapmotor and Xiaomi are driving competition with ultra-fast development cycles, software-first design and latest battery technology. That’s prompting legacy brands to overhaul their production systems to keep pace.

Suzuki, which pulled out of the US and Chinese markets in 2012 and 2018, is looking to India as its biggest growth engine.

The maker of the Jimny compact SUV plans to grow its production capacity there to four million units by 2030, from less than three million this year. The company expects the India car market to double or triple in size within the next few decades.

See also: Mining giant Rio Tinto plans to expand metals trading business

title: India lets wealth-focused funds with US$463 bil invest abroad
article:
(Sept 25): India’s market regulator will allow a US$463 billion ($592 billion) segment of its portfolio management industry catering to wealthy individuals to invest in overseas securities and short equity options for the first time, as part of a sweeping overhaul of the rules.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will also allow the funds to invest in unlisted debt securities and take exchange-traded derivatives exposure of up to 1.25 times clients’ assets, it said after a board meeting on Thursday. Portfolio managers can also take unhedged short positions up to a prescribed limit, which the regulator didn’t specify.

The changes significantly expand investment options for an industry that has grown rapidly in recent years as wealthy Indians seek professionally managed, customised products. Known as portfolio management services, or PMS, the industry oversaw about 44.4 trillion rupees ($592 billion) as of August, up from 40 trillion rupees a year earlier, Sebi data showed.

The move also gives wealthy Indians another route to global markets, where demand for artificial-intelligence (AI) stocks has surged. The country already allows individuals to invest in foreign securities directly, while mutual fund can invest abroad subject to a regulatory limit. The new rules come as persistent foreign outflows have pressured the rupee against the dollar.

The changes “expand the opportunity across global investments, unlisted investment-grade debt, and the use of derivatives to manage risk”, said Dharmendra Jain, a co-founder of Ionic Wealth, an arm of stock broker Angel One Ltd.

See also: UBS brings institutional-grade investment access to Asia private wealth clients

Foreign investments in equity and debt will be allowed through the liberalised remittance scheme (LRS), which allow resident Indians to send up to US$250,000 each financial year, Sebi said. Mutual funds, by contrast, remain constrained by a US$7 billion limit exhausted several years ago.

Indians remitted US$457 million via the LRS route in June, data published by the Reserve Bank of India last month showed.

The overhaul follows a consultation paper floated by Sebi in July.

See also: Turkiye arrests Tera chairman at heart of funds scandal

Meanwhile, allowing portfolio managers to express a bearish view on a stock through unhedged options wagers could also support volumes at Indian bourses, where growth has slowed following years of curbs by the regulator to dim speculative trading.

Sebi also approved a new ‘mutual fund-only’ PMS product with a minimum investment of 2.5 million rupees, half the five-million-rupee ticket size for a regular PMS product.

Separately, the regulator allowed foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) to trade non-cash-settled, non-agricultural commodity derivatives, a move aimed at broadening market participation. Such instruments have recently enjoyed increased activity from retail investors.

Participation will depend on ensuring that FPIs exit the trade before the delivery obligation arises, the regulator said.

title: US tech titans, Trump fete Xi at lavish state dinner
article:
(Sept 25): Luminaries from Wall Street and Silicon Valley joined President Donald Trump for a state dinner honouring his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, in a demonstration of US technological and financial might.

Trump has welcomed Xi with fanfare this week, affording rare state visit honours to a counterpart considered one of America’s biggest industrial and military rivals. The race to dominate in artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a growing flashpoint, with Chinese companies rapidly closing the gap with US models.

Even as they compete, both governments are agreed on pushing ahead with AI’s development despite mounting concerns over the technology’s impact on jobs, the environment and even the future of humanity.

Thursday’s dinner brought together some of the most influential names in that sphere. Xi was seated with Trump at a table with Nvidia Corp’s Jensen Huang, whose best semiconductors the US has banned from being exported to China. Others at that table included Apple Inc’s Tim Cook and Lisa Su of chip giant Advanced Micro Devices Inc.

By contrast, at the banquet Beijing held for Trump earlier this year the American guest of honour was seated exclusively with relatives as well as officials from the US and Chinese delegations.

See also: Goldman’s Moe says he’s in ‘stronger-for-longer camp’ on AI

Jeff Bezos, the founder of Amazon.com Inc, and his wife Lauren Sanchez Bezos.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other top Trump advisers on trade and the economy, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Energy Secretary Chris Wright and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, were on the guest list, as was Federal Reserve chairman Kevin Warsh. Other invitees on Thursday included tech icons Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk as well as OpenAI’s Sam Altman.

Trump’s warm welcome for Xi, however, has also drawn criticism, including from a Republican senator, Roger Wicker of Mississippi, who questioned the administration’s decision to salute China’s leader. As guests arrived on Thursday, protesters near the White House could be heard chanting, including calls to “Free Hong Kong” and “Free Tibet”.

See also: Meta’s best month since 2013 has it on cusp of US$2 tril level

Trump and first lady Melania Trump welcomed Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan. The US first lady wore what appeared to be a white top with a large bow and black pants, while Madame Peng wore a red long-sleeved dress.

Finance executives on the guest list for the evening included Jane Fraser of Citigroup Inc, Jamie Dimon of JPMorgan Chase & Co, Stephen Schwarzman of Blackstone Inc, David Solomon of Goldman Sachs Group Inc and Mastercard Inc’s Michael Miebach. Other business titans invited included Kelly Ortberg of Boeing Co and David Ellison of Paramount Skydance Corp.

Noticeably absent however was the presence of any Chinese business leaders. Xi’s delegation was not expected to include many chief executive officers, highlighting potential differences in expectations between the countries about the summit, even as Trump said he expected to secure many business deals. Of the more than 130 names on the guest list, only 19 were part of the Chinese delegation — and none were business figures.

Before the soiree, Trump cast the dinner as the hottest ticket in town, saying “everybody wanted to be there”, and describing the guest list as encompassing “the entire tech world, the entire banking world, and a lot more”.

State dinners are a grand White House tradition for honouring foreign leaders. It’s the second such celebration of Trump’s current term, following a dinner in April for King Charles III and his wife, Queen Camilla.

Guests will be served three courses, including a yellow squash velouté, sesame-crusted sea bass and vanilla crémeux served alongside honey ice cream. The first lady’s office described the menu as showcasing “American ingredients with subtle Chinese influence”.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

It will open with a toast of Schramsberg “Blanc De Noirs”, a California sparkling wine, the White House said. A wine from the vineyard was also served at president Richard Nixon’s groundbreaking visit to Beijing in 1972.

Attendees will be entertained by Christopher Macchio, a tenor who also performed at Trump’s 2025 inauguration, as well as military bands. The decor for the lavish dinner highlighted the colour red, an auspicious colour in Chinese culture, with urns topped with red blossoms and red linens dressing tables also adorned with seasonal dahlias and ranunculus.

While expectations for breakthroughs were low going into the summit, the countries will extend a trade truce — that was set to expire in November — until Jan 10. Trump said before Thursday’s meetings that he and Xi would discuss issues related to security, technology and AI. Xi later told Trump their countries could continue to have a dialogue on AI and jointly guard against misuse of the technology, according to the official Xinhua News Agency.

Both Trump and Xi cited the long history of US-China ties and what they cast as a friendship that has endured — remarks that resonated following a turbulent stretch in the relationship between the two nations.

The US president in his toast said the two countries had “never gotten along better since the first trade ships from New York left the harbour to arrive on the banks of the Pearl River”, and expressed optimism that they could both find “prosperity and security for future generations”.

Xi referenced the cooperation between the US and China during World War II, noting that the Chinese people rescued hundreds of American pilots at the cost of many lives. “Such a friendship, forged in blood and fire, will surely live on through the generations,” he said.

Trump’s efforts to ban three news organisations also affected coverage of the summit. Even after the White House restored access to the outlets, though, the White House did not say publicly if it planned to reinstate CNN to a rotating pool of networks that handle presidential coverage, a sticking point in a media boycott.

The president had made his anticipation for Xi’s visit clear for months — and regularly cited events such as the state dinner as justification for plans to construct a massive ballroom on the White House grounds. Trump has claimed the White House lacks the space to host such large events.

In his toast, the president invited the state dinner attendees to visit the still-under-construction ballroom, calling it a “special treat” in honour of Xi’s visit. “You will be the first people” on the ballroom floor, Trump said.

title: Growth minister says Japan has exited reflationary phase
article:
(Sept 25): Japan no longer needs a reflationary policy of aggressive monetary easing and nimble fiscal spending, according to Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi, one of the Cabinet’s most aggressive reflationists.

“The era of ‘Abenomics-style’ reflationary policies — which involved aggressively easing monetary policy and taking a flexible approach to fiscal policy — is over,” Kiuchi said at a press conference on Friday.

He also noted that Japan is no longer in “an era of monetary easing”, but has entered a phase in which prices are gradually rising and interest rates are climbing.

Kiuchi’s comments follow renewed weakness in the yen and further gains in government bond yields this week. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama separately said that US President Donald Trump had conveyed his concern over the yen during his meeting with Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi earlier this week.

The salvo of comments by senior officials on Friday gave the impression that the government was looking to shore up the currency and reassure investors concerned about Takaichi’s spending plans. The yen gained after Katayama’s comments to briefly hit 158.33 against the dollar, but still remains close to levels that could spur Tokyo to intervene in the currency market again.

The remarks by Kiuchi echo recent comments by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. Bessent has urged Japan to move away from the reflationary policies associated with Abenomics, the economic strategy initiated by the late prime minister Shinzo Abe.

See also: Japan's central bank hikes rates in split decision after US pressure

Kiuchi sought to draw a distinction between Abenomics and the current policy mix under Takaichi, while reiterating the government’s position that Japan has yet to decisively emerge from deflation.

“If you view Abenomics and Sanae-nomics as essentially the same thing, I would appreciate it if you could understand my remarks to mean that the latter is not reflationary policy,” he said. “I understand that we have not yet fully escaped deflation.”

Kiuchi was retained in a Cabinet reshuffle last week. That helped signal policy continuity for Takaichi’s administration, but it also kept fuelling the view among some market analysts that the government is still looking to pursue a loose fiscal policy while trying to slow down interest rate hikes by the Bank of Japan (BOJ).

See also: PGIM turns more selective on Japan real estate as rates climb

The BOJ raised its policy rate last week at a meeting attended by Kiuchi. Bessent has strongly hinted at the need for the BOJ to raise interest rates to help the yen find an appropriate level.

title: Trump-Xi summit goes big on pomp but small on substance
article:
(Sept 25): Donald Trump’s fete for Chinese leader Xi Jinping has been heavy on pageantry and platitudes but light on substantive announcements, with the events shadowed by the US president’s preoccupation with construction projects and personal grievances.

Through Thursday evening in Washington, the most significant news tied to the gathering was announced before it even began, when US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said just as Xi’s plane landed that the two sides had extended a trade truce for another two months.

Anticipated agreements on tariff cuts and a new line of communication on artificial intelligence (AI) have yet to be announced, and Chinese stocks in Hong Kong declined, suggesting traders saw a lack of progress. The day was capped off by a state dinner featuring a three-course menu, attended by American tech and financial titans.

Trump gifted Xi a statue of a bald eagle — a national symbol of the US — and declared he and Xi have “never gotten along better”. He then appeared to venture off-script, inviting dinner guests to tour the construction site of his White House ballroom. Xi offered a gauzy history of US-China ties in his dinner toast that papered over historic tensions.

It’s not as if the two leaders lacked contentious issues to iron out. In the months before the summit, China has been accused of undercutting the US at home and abroad.

Trump alleged in a July prime-time address that China carried out the “largest compromise of election data in history”. Weapons inspectors discovered evidence that Iran-backed Houthi militants have used components shipped from China to manufacture weapons in Yemen. China continues to buy Iranian crude and is holding F-35 stealth aircraft parts shipped to Hong Kong under unclear circumstances.

See also: Trump and Xi buy time on trade with neither able to afford a fight

But throughout the day, Trump repeatedly cast Xi as a friend rather than the US’ foremost geopolitical rival despite their nations’ intensifying competition on AI and divides over trade.

Kicking off three hours of events at the White House, Trump hailed his “truly great friendship” with Xi, saying “there’s much we can achieve”. Still, expectations were low going into the summit that it would produce breakthroughs on major disagreements.

Xi was less effusive, focusing on policy objectives, including pushing Trump to consider more collaboration to ensure AI remains “under human control”. Trump has dismissed the notion that AI poses a threat.

See also: US unveils two-month truce extension as Xi lands for summit

“China keeps its door wide open, welcomes American companies wanting to invest and do business there. We hope Chinese companies are treated fairly here in the United States,” Xi said.

The Chinese leader also prodded Trump to change Washington’s long-standing position on Taiwan, according to Beijing. The White House has yet to release its own official description of the meeting.

The summit thus far has been a gift to Xi, as he received a warm welcome from a US president who thus far has struggled to regain leverage since the two countries’ trade war last year. The two leaders are scheduled to have tea and tour the National Archives on Friday before Xi’s departure.

Also on display at the White House were myriad controversies and distractions that have marked Trump’s second year back in power.

No major US television network aired live footage of the leaders meeting. Typically, such a summit would dominate the airwaves, but networks have mostly declined to broadcast video of Trump since the president banned cable channels CNN, MS NOW and online outlet Politico from the White House.

Reporters from those outlets were reinstated under a federal judge’s order after they filed a lawsuit alleging the ban violated their constitutional rights.

The TV-obsessed president groused about the blackout on social media, accusing the outlets of declining to air footage of the “magnificent” summit because “they didn’t want credit to be given to Trump”. Among those not broadcasting footage was Trump-friendly Fox News.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Trump also mocked his predecessor Joe Biden in front of Xi while showing him gold-framed photos of past presidents that he had installed on the historic White House colonnade. In place of Biden’s photo is an autopen. Critics called the move inappropriate.

After their meeting, Trump showed Xi the stone helipad he had installed on the South Lawn and said Xi “loves good granite”. He even brought the Chinese leader inside the presidential helicopter. During an afternoon gap in the schedule, construction crews’ heavy machinery clanged in the distance as they worked on the ballroom.

The contrast to Xi’s last state visit, in 2015, was stark. Then-US president Barack Obama held a press conference with Xi, at which he painstakingly described their agenda. The American leader said that included a “frank discussion” on human rights.

Trump made no mention of that topic on Thursday and ignored journalists’ shouted questions about jailed Hong Kong democracy activist Jimmy Lai.

In Trump’s first term, his team worked on plans to address allegations of Chinese intellectual property theft and far-reaching trade agreements involving a broader swath of issues than the current truce.

Trump blamed China for the spread of Covid-19 in 2020 and called it the “China virus”. This week, he praised Xi for the red-carpet treatment he received in Beijing in May and has offered him the same in Washington.

Some of Trump’s fellow Republicans criticised the president’s approach, saying it undercuts the promises he made during his 2024 campaign to get tough on China.

“The president campaigned on an anti-China policy,” said North Carolina Senator Thom Tillis. “You go look at those MAGA rallies and look at everybody cheering when he said he’s going to take it to China.”

title: US, Iran said to be exploring phased deal to reopen Hormuz
article:
(Sept 25): US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a phased deal that would see Tehran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and Washington lift its blockade of Iranian ports, according to a person familiar with the discussions.

The two countries — which have both refused to make similar agreements in recent months — were making a push for a breakthrough Thursday on the sidelines of the United Nations (UN) General Assembly, the person said, declining to be named discussing private matters. Qatari officials are mediating the negotiations.

A sequenced deal would be similar to the memorandum of understanding that the US and Iran struck in mid-June, which led to a fragile ceasefire that collapsed just weeks later.

A White House official said President Donald Trump remains open to talking with Iran but stressed the US didn’t need to negotiate because it was in a strong position as a result of an escalating sanctions campaign and an ongoing naval blockade pressuring Iran’s economy.

Talks about a potential phased deal were reported earlier Thursday by Reuters.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told a group of journalists and academics in New York that his country offered the US a new seven-day proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz if certain conditions were met, the Financial Times reported.

See also: Suez Canal revival gathers pace as Hormuz crisis reroutes ships

Oil fell on reports that US and Iranian negotiators were exploring a phased deal, with global benchmark Brent sliding towards US$106 ($136) a barrel after rising more than 7% over the previous two days.

Off-and-on negotiations between Washington and Tehran have broken down numerous times since the war began, mostly over disagreements related to the Strait of Hormuz and when Iran would get access to billions in funds frozen by the US.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, who was in New York for the UN summit, used his speech to stress Tehran wouldn’t allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a US naval blockade remain in place.

See also: Trump says US starting ‘economic warfare’ operation against Iran

Araghchi represented Tehran in the talks and outlined its “firm positions” on reopening Hormuz, according to Iranian state media. Those conditions include the US immediately lifting a naval blockade, unfreezing Iranian assets and ending the war “on all fronts”, according to Iranian reports, an apparent reference to Israel’s campaign against Iran-backed Hezbollah militants in Lebanon.

“We have not closed the Strait of Hormuz,” Pezeshkian said in an interview with Fox News broadcast on Thursday evening. “It was open without any legal justification or framework. They attacked us.”

Trump told reporters on Tuesday that US and Iranian officials had spoken in New York amid the flurry of UN meetings. His comments lifted stocks and pushed down oil prices.

The American president has repeatedly said the US and Iran were close to a deal with no results. He’s also threatened Tehran with military escalation multiple times — including a threat to “annihilate” the country earlier this week — without following through.

White House special envoy Steve Witkoff said on social media this week that mediators had spent much of the day shuttling between US and Iranian officials during extended discussions.

title: Xi pushes Trump to ‘oppose’ Taiwan independence in rare call
article:
(Sept 25): Chinese leader Xi Jinping pressed the US to outright “oppose” Taiwan independence, marking his first public call for President Donald Trump to change Washington’s decades-old stance on the self-ruled island.

During their inaugural White House summit on Thursday, Xi urged the US leader to “adhere to the correct position of opposing Taiwan independence”, according to the official Xinhua News Agency. That wording is stronger than the Biden administration’s previous statement that US officials “do not support” the island seeking formal independence.

Since coming to power in 2012, Xi has made bringing Taiwan under China’s control a key goal and vowed to achieve it someday, by force if necessary. As the Chinese leader heads towards an expected fourth term in office, he’s ramping up diplomatic pressure to isolate the democratic chip hub and block future weapons sales from Washington.

The US still hasn’t released a readout from the meeting, which lasted less than two hours, meaning it isn’t clear how Trump responded to Xi’s request. China privately asked the Trump administration to declare it “opposes” Taiwan independence back in 2025, a person familiar with the matter said at the time.

The White House didn’t respond to a request for comments.

See also: Modi plans Canada trip for trade deal, speeds up Mexico talks

“While this may appear a semantic shift, the impact would be meaningful,” said Bloomberg Economics’ Jennifer Welch, who served as the director for China and Taiwan on the National Security Council under the previous Biden and Trump administrations. China would use any switch in language from Trump to undermine Taiwan’s confidence in US support, she added.

“Opposing Taiwan independence implies an active effort to contain what Beijing sees as pro-independence forces,” Welch said.

Trump has already delayed a planned US$14 billion ($17.9 billion) arms package for Taiwan for months. After his last meeting with Xi in Beijing, Trump described that deal as “a very good negotiating chip” for the US — remarks that rattled Taipei. Any change in wording would fan concerns that Washington’s position on the democracy of 23 million people is becoming a bargaining chip in US-China ties.

See also: Traders eye Xi-Trump meet for clues on AI rivalry, yuan outlook

Xi has rarely made such an explicit call to an American leader. The last time came in November 2024, when he told outgoing president Joe Biden if the US wanted peace it should “oppose Taiwan independence”, during their final face-to-face.

Chinese state media released Xi’s remarks on Taiwan hours before its full readout on Thursday, throwing a spotlight on Beijing’s top red line issue. That followed a similar pattern to the last Trump-Xi summit in May, when China warned mishandling the Taiwan issue could lead to "clashes" between the superpowers in a statement issued while talks were ongoing.

Xi entered his first state visit to America in 11 years emboldened after last year exposing US reliance on China’s rare earths, a move that enabled Beijing to push back against Trump’s triple-digit tariffs. Those minerals are critical for making everything from missiles to mobile phones and have been key in keeping a lid on further US export controls.

Trump has given Xi an unprecedented welcome, becoming the first US president to greet a Chinese counterpart on the tarmac. The Republican leader will host only his second state dinner of this term for Xi — one of America’s biggest economic and military rivals.

In a boon to Beijing, Trump’s comments on Taiwan have marked a departure from Biden, who claimed he had defend the island from any invasion by China. The Republican leader has urged officials in Taipei to step up their ability to defend themselves.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Handling the Taiwan question with prudence will “lay a solid foundation for strategic cooperation between China and the US”, Xi said on Thursday.

Ryan Hass, a director of the China Center at the Brookings Institution in Washington, said Xi was trying to link the concept of “constructive strategic stability” to opposing Taiwan independence. That slogan was unveiled by Chinese officials at the leaders’ summit in May to define a new era in ties.

“The key acid test will be what Trump says on Taiwan,” Hass added. “Not just what Xi urges Trump to endorse.”

title: SIA Engineering finds itself on firmer footing post-Covid
article:
What company should you invest in if you want to leverage Singapore’s position as a world-class aviation hub? Some might recommend taking a position in Singapore Airlines (SIA), the city-state’s national carrier. But given how SIA’s stock price has doubled since the lows of the Covid-19 pandemic days, investors hungry for capital gains might be better off looking elsewhere — perhaps a company that is positioned within the same aviation value chain but primed for further growth.

As it turns out, there is a Mainboard-listed company that fits the bill: SIA Engineering Company (SIAEC).

Established as a subsidiary company of SIA in 1992, SIAEC was originally the airline’s engineering division. Since its inception, the company has dedicated much time and resources to develop its capacity and capabilities for next-generation aircraft, and to grow its geographical presence as a maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) provider. Today, SIAEC operates across six hangars in Singapore and an additional three hangars in Clark, Philippines. Earlier in May, it announced the official opening of a new base maintenance facility in Subang, Malaysia. The two-hangar facility, with the second hangar expected to be operational in the second half of FY2026/27, further expands SIAEC’s base maintenance network within the region.

While airlines are exposed to the vagaries of seasonal travel patterns, MRO providers like SIAEC have a relatively more stable business model. Afterall, every aircraft needs to go through maintenance to be fit for flight. This will always be the case, whether or not an airline is able to fill up its planes with passengers.

That strategic position appears to have been recognised by the markets. SIAEC’s stock has rallied significantly in the past year, going up by nearly 90% from around $2 in April 2025 to $3.75 in November 2025. The stock continues to trade at above $3, closing at $3.14 on Sept 23.

See also: Cosco readies for growth as efficient, reliable, end-to-end logistics provider in Southeast Asia

The turnaround in fortunes comes as a surprise considering how disruptive the Covid-19 pandemic was for SIAEC’s business. Strict border entry restrictions saw a near halt in global air travel. As a result, most airlines opted to store their grounded aircraft instead of flying them. To avoid layoffs, SIAEC executives and managers took pay cuts of between 5% to 30%.

While painful, SIAEC CEO Chin Yau Seng says the Covid-19 pandemic ended up paving the way for today’s booming MRO market. The longtime SIA executive was named CEO-designate on June 1, 2023 before assuming the role fully on Oct 1, 2023.

Before joining SIAEC, Chin was SIA’s senior vice president for cargo. The SIA scholar earned degrees in accounting & finance, and operational research at the London School of Economics and Political Science before starting work at the airline. Chin’s career in aviation has seen him take on a wide variety of roles, including serving as chief executive of SilkAir and Tiger Airways Holdings, SIA’s former subsidiaries.

See also: Wee Hur’s plan to become more than a builder

“Coming out of Covid, there were both challenges and opportunities,” Chin says. “We were quite happy to see a lot of flight activity returning and of course, with flight activity returning, there was a great demand for manpower to support all the additional flights.”

Even till today, the market for aviation talent and manpower continues to remain tight. The collapse in demand for air travel during the pandemic caused many suppliers and sub-suppliers for aerospace manufacturers to either pivot or shutter their operations. Even though new suppliers are coming in, they would need to obtain the necessary qualifications from regulators in order to do business. This, Chin says, poses a huge constraint on supply chains as spare parts are in short supply.

“With the supply lag, it meant that the whole system was overheated,” Chin says, “For us, it was both an impact and opportunity. On one hand, there is an impact because the aircraft had to stay in the hangars for longer. This means we could not induct other aircraft earlier. But, on the other hand, because the supply chain is constrained, it drove a huge rise in demand for repairs, and we are in the repair and MRO business.”

The demand for MRO services is even higher than in the pre-Covid-19 days. For one, airlines who want to recover their grounded planes for use will need to go through quite a bit of maintenance work to return them to the skies again. In addition, the pandemic resulted in delivery delays for newer aircraft models. As such, older planes still have to be flown in the interim.

“Some of the new aircraft orders are coming in late, so you need to fly the older aircraft for a longer period, which actually means more maintenance. You are going through some of the heavy cycles for the aircraft that you would have potentially retired if the new aircraft had come in,” Chin explains.

That is one of the reasons why, under Chin’s leadership, SIAEC has sought to expand its hangar capacity by going into Subang. Today, 70% to 80% of SIAEC’s base maintenance business comes from its parent company SIA, with the remainder from other airlines.

With Subang, Chin says SIAEC will be able to redirect some of their work for SIA there, thus freeing up more space for other customers. The extra space means SIAEC will be able to operate more specialised lines at its hangars for specific aircraft models.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“For instance, today we are sending to Subang all the [Airbus] A350s. So, you will have dedicated A350 lines. When you have dedicated lines, productivity typically increases because this is low mix but higher volume. So, you actually churn your resources a lot more efficiently,” Chin says.

“One of the challenges, when we are doing so much of the work with constrained capacity in Singapore, is that you have to mix the lines because the demand is just so high. You want to make use of every bit of hangar time and you will see that our hangars are actually quite full.”

On top of that, Chin wants to raise SIAEC’s overall productivity through a new framework they are implementing called the Enterprise Operating System (EOS). Launched in 2024 and expected to be completed at all key operational business units by the end of FY2026/27, EOS seeks to revamp the way SIAEC goes about its operations by bringing together Lean management principles, digital tools, and AI.

“With the EOS programme, what we are trying to do is to look at the end-to-end process and do a few things. Number one, what work is more regular? We want that to be done like clockwork. That means if we set it out to be 10 days, no matter what, we will be able to churn out the aircraft in 10 days, despite some of the challenges,” Chin says.

Understanding the entire operational process is critical when it comes to managing supply chain disruptions, which is becoming increasingly common in the volatile world we live in today.

“There are various interventions we can do when things go a little off. If spares don’t come on time, how do we rejig the sequence of the check such that we can still deliver within 10 days? When there are real big disruptions, what are the interventions we can do and build into our process and system? That means for every known disruption, we actually have a remedy for it,” Chin says.

“This EOS is really about stringing together processes to make sure that despite all these supply chain challenges, we can still keep to our rhythm and make sure we do it with optimal manpower.”

Not just an SIA offshoot

Even though SIA is the largest shareholder of SIAEC, holding a nearly 78% stake in the company, Chin says the company actually serves a wide mix of clients. When it comes to flight handling, SIAEC serves other carriers as well besides SIA.

“Flight handling takes place when the aircraft comes in and goes out,” Chin says. “You certify the aircraft. You do some of the basic water toilet servicing. That business is very diversified.”

Even then, SIA remains SIAEC’s largest client, Chin adds. “Everything that is done on the tarmac, when the aircraft are overnighting in Singapore, that is what we call maintenance operations at line maintenance. Typically, you serve the base carrier, which in this case is SIA and Scoot. That part is almost entirely SIA Group, but it is also true of many other airports where there is some MRO servicing a base carrier. That’s just the nature of operations.”

To diversify its business, SIAEC maintains an extensive portfolio of 26 subsidiaries and joint ventures with leading engine and component original equipment manufacturers and other partners. Back in 2001, SIAEC started a 50:50 joint venture company with Rolls-Royce, Singapore Aero Engine Services (SAESL). SAESL is currently in the process of expanding its capacity via a new engine repair facility in Loyang as well as redevelopment works at Rolls-Royce’s existing facilities at Seletar Aerospace Park.

SIAEC’s diversified business was the reason why it was not seriously affected by the tensions in Iran, Chin says. “Some of our line maintenance operations and our joint ventures do serve Middle Eastern carriers and we were hit initially but as things settled, they flew again. Some of the initial lost business has been recovered.”

Chin wants to take SIAEC to greater heights and enter new markets. Earlier, on July 3, the company signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MOU) with Air India to potentially set up an MRO joint venture (JV) in India.

“We need to execute well. There is nothing without challenges. India’s market, for instance, is not easy and I think it will call on every bit of our resources to make it work. But I think we have the right people and expertise. We will have to learn very fast,” Chin says.

“There’s all these opportunities for us to tap on, and we have been taking advantage of that. Of course, with most of this, there is some lead time, there is investment cost, but what we are doing is we are securing the growth story of SIAEC.”

Any questions for SIAEC? Ask us here or scan to submit your question.

title: Homegrown EGP Energy eyes overseas expansion to power growth as shares climb after IPO
article:
From lights to air-conditioning, from smartphones to artificial intelligence, electricity powers many facets of daily life. Put simply, an electricity grid that delivers power from generators to consumers is essential to modern life and economies.

In Singapore, EGP Energy Corporation is one such company, building and maintaining the national grid to ensure an efficient and reliable electricity supply to end users. A home-grown company, EGP Energy is a key provider of electrical infrastructure solutions and services for electrical transmission and distribution (T&D) projects in Singapore.

Since its debut on the Mainboard of Singapore’s stock exchange on July 29, the counter has risen to 74 cents on Sept 22, up 19% from its IPO price of 51 cents, making it the only stock listed in 2026 to trade above its IPO price.

For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, the company reported a 180% y-o-y rise in patmi to $6.07 million, on revenue of $30.7 million, which is a 157% increase from the previous corresponding period.

On Sept 17, UOB Kay Hian analysts Tang Kai Jie and John Cheong initiated coverage with a “buy” rating and a target price of 92 cents. They believe in the company’s business model, noting its “superior unit economics and asset-light model” and point out that its 20.3% 2026 ebitda margin is above the engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning (EPCC) peer average of 15.2%.

EGP Energy traces its roots to 1992, when executive chairman Frankie Fan founded his electrical engineering business in Singapore, Tong Guan Resources (TGR), which supplied electrical contractors with quality medium voltage (MV) cables and secondary components. TGR has since been renamed EGP Vision (EGPV). EGP Energy fully owns EGP Smart Energy (EGPSE), which holds a 76.9% stake in EGPV.

See also: Thai billionaire revives Vietnam gas projects in overseas push

A mechanical engineering graduate from the Nanjing Institute of Technology, Fan has over 30 years of experience in the electrical infrastructure industry in Singapore, China, Indonesia, Vietnam, India, Egypt and Brunei.

“I came to Singapore around 1992,” recounts Fan, who earned an MBA from the National University of Singapore in 1998. “I had stayed in Singapore before, so I know Singapore very well and like this place a lot.”

In 2000, Fan and his company completed their first substantial engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) project to supply a gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) for a 66kV substation in Singapore.

See also: Thailand maps plan to source 89% of power from clean energy

The company has since gone from strength to strength, building its capabilities and reputation and securing new projects for Singapore’s grid development. In 2003, the firm won an EPC project for a 400kV substation in Singapore, the highest-voltage T&D asset at the time. This project was the first extra high-voltage (EHV)/ high-voltage (HV) substation in Singapore and is still in use.

Fan shares that the customer awarding projects to the company was “very smart” in how it assessed potential vendors. “The customer gave us a chance, but it was for a relatively small and remote site [and] that way, even if something went wrong, it wouldn’t impact the main grid,” says Fan.

Today, EGP Energy’s business is divided into two segments along the power market value chain. First, under the T&D projects segment, it specialises in providing EPC management services for T&D projects, including project design, supply, installation, positioning, and testing and commissioning of electrical equipment spanning GIS, transmission cables, transformers, protection and control systems, and spare parts across the EHV and HV spectrum. The company also provides consultancy services on various aspects of T&D projects and project management.

Under its maintenance and servicing (M&S) segment, the firm offers inspections, testing and diagnostics, cleaning and servicing, condition monitoring, troubleshooting, equipment replacement and emergency repairs for T&D assets.

For FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025, T&D projects accounted for approximately 52.9%, 57.3% and 54.0% of the company’s revenue, respectively. Meanwhile, M&S contributed 47.1%, 42.7% and 46.0% of company revenue in these three years.

As the company’s non-manufacturing asset-light model involves sourcing multi-OEM equipment, capex is minimal at 2% of revenue, notes Tang and Cheong, who also point out that the company’s maintenance and servicing (M&S) contracts are recurring and generate robust 50% gross margins.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

The company is also in a net cash position and has recommended paying out 40% of net profit after tax as dividends for FY2026 and FY2027, according to its IPO prospectus.

From a competitive standpoint, the company states that it has established “strong relationships” with key stakeholders in the T&D project supply chain. This strengthens its ability to secure projects, source equipment with compressed timelines, execute projects efficiently and respond to evolving industry requirements.

According to an independent market research report by business consultancy Frost & Sullivan, EGP Energy has established a “strong competitive” position within Singapore’s EHV and HV T&D market, particularly in the switchgear and transformer segments. The company held nearly 25% of the EHV and HV switchgear and transformer segments, with a market-leading share of 37.5% for the EHV and HV switchgear segment, representing more than one-third of all 66kV, 230kV and 400kV switchgear contracts awarded in Singapore during the year.

EGP Energy is only one of 16 firms that hold the L6 SY04 unlimited bidding category under the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) registration framework. This is the highest contractor qualification in Singapore’s T&D market, characterised by substantial barriers to entry that protect the reliability, safety, and technical integrity of the national power grid.

Stringent approval and pre-qualification requirements, along with elevated technical, safety, and compliance standards that significantly increase the engineering complexity, expertise, and cost of T&D projects, make it challenging for new entrants and foreign players to break into the market and limit the number of qualified contractors capable of undertaking complex T&D projects in Singapore.

“Transmission failures can affect an entire zone and if a major issue occurred, it could mean Singapore might have no electricity,” says Fan. “This could be extremely serious and so the customer’s strict requirements are necessary.”

The firm’s capabilities include expertise in engineering requirements and the application of advanced technologies across T&D projects, such as gas-insulated lines used in T&D infrastructure, sensors for real-time visibility for grid monitoring and control, and automated distribution management systems as part of distribution management. More significantly, the company can integrate these technologies to strengthen the reliability, efficiency, and performance of the T&D systems it builds.

A key technical differentiator between EGP Energy and its peers is the firm’s ability to integrate equipment from multiple original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) within a single substation. This includes complex mixed-OEM 230kV GIS extensions, enabling compliance with bespoke utility specifications that single-OEM-aligned contractors or OEMs cannot readily address.

In addition, subsidiary EGPSE was among the first to introduce predictive diagnostic monitoring (PDM) solutions in Singapore’s transmission network, and this early adoption remains a core technical differentiator. PDM solutions on EHV equipment underpin the reliability of Singapore’s grid by providing continuous real-time detection of insulation degradation to enable predictive maintenance.

To fund EGP Energy’s expansion, the company tapped Singapore’s capital markets with a stock exchange listing. In addition to the public tranche, cornerstone investors include Amova Asset Management, Avanda Investment Management, among others. Amova and Avanda are two of nine selected fund managers for Singapore’s Equity Market Development Programme (EQDP).

The company successfully raised $30.6 million in gross proceeds to fund the expansion of its product offerings and into Malaysia and Indonesia. The proceeds are also slated to enhance the company’s capabilities and support general corporate and working capital purposes.

On Sept 15, following through on its intention to venture overseas, EGP Energy announced its expansion into Malaysia through subsidiary EGP Infrastructure Investments (EGPII), which entered into a joint venture agreement with Kum Fatt Engineering (KFE), a wholly owned subsidiary of Malaysia-listed UUE Holdings.

Under the collaboration, EGPII will hold a 60% equity stake in the joint venture, with KFE holding the remaining 40%; KFE is a grade G7 contractor registered with the Construction Industry Development Board. A G7 contractor has no upper limit on the contract value of projects it can tender for or undertake.

Fan says that the joint venture is an “important first step” in the company’s overseas expansion. “Malaysia’s grid investment cycle is entering a period of sustained growth, and by partnering with KFE, we gain an established local partner with relevant market knowledge and project experience in Malaysia,” adds Fan.

Executive director Nicholas Fan adds that Malaysia and Indonesia are “promising” markets. “We are basically looking at them from a strategic perspective, but the pace of development will be different due to different environments, landscapes and geographical conditions,” he adds.

Despite its overseas ambitions, EGP Energy remains committed to Singapore. As at Sept 1, EGP Energy’s order book stood at $305.1 million, with projects slated for progressive completion through 2031. All these projects are in Singapore.

Furthermore, as a leading T&D contractor, the company is well positioned to seize future opportunities as the Singapore government has committed to a multi-decade capex spending on infrastructure, including in areas such as transport and energy storage. The independent market research report also cites that Singapore’s overall electricity demand is projected to increase, with system peak demand rising by 2.8% and 4.7% from 2025 to 2030.

“Based on the tenders we are participating in, we believe there is still a lot of room at the end-distribution level, because you need replacement and additional transformers, more switchgear, more cables,” says Nicholas.

“Our idea and goal moving forward remain the same: we want to remain an essential support partner to our [Singapore] customers and continue to build upon our strong foundation in Singapore.”

title: Hong Kong’s Buy&Ship eyes Tokyo listing in Japan expansion push
article:
(Sept 25): Buy&Ship is the first Hong Kong-based company chosen by the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) to join its initial public offering (IPO) incubation programme, giving it a hand in expanding its presence in Japan.

The cross-border online shopping platform operator is still in the IPO planning stage and the TSE is but one option, co-founder and chief executive officer Sheldon Li said in an interview Thursday.

“Being chosen by the TSE to join the startup hub actually speeds things up for us,” said Li, who added that the company aims to bolster business in Japan as 45% of transactions come from the country.

The TSE Asia Startup Hub programme launched in 2024 as a way to encourage companies from around Asia to list in Tokyo, which has seen its IPO numbers decline. Participating companies stand to receive business development and fundraising assistance alongside support for their share sales and listings, according to the Japan Exchange Group, which operates the exchange.

Japan’s first-time share offerings have raised a meager ¥232 billion (US$1.5 billion) so far this year, the lowest amount for the first nine months since 2022. In contrast, proceeds for Hong Kong, which is in the midst of an IPO boom, were many times higher at US$45 billion over the same period, according to Bloomberg-compiled data.

When asked what the company would use proceeds from an IPO for, Li said: “Building infrastructure is one, and building out the US business is also one huge opportunity for us and we haven’t tapped into it yet.”

See also: SoftBank-backed Carro said to mull first dual Nasdaq-SGX IPO

title: Singapore judge raises doubts Radiant World is owed US$1 bil
article:
(Sept 25): A Singapore judge has cast doubt on trader Radiant World’s claim that it is owed more than US$1 billion ($1.28 billion) from customers, citing concerns over an alleged “pattern of fraudulent conduct”, according to a court filing.

Radiant World, battling demands from creditors, was placed under interim judicial management on Thursday, when the High Court appointed KPMG restructuring executives to take charge of the business. The decision, granting an application by Mizuho Bank Ltd, opens a new chapter in a saga that has gripped the global commodities industry.

In the ruling, judge Kristy Tan concluded the company was or was likely to become unable to pay its debts, according to a signed copy seen by Bloomberg. Tan added in the document that she placed “little weight” on the company’s claims it is owed US$1 billion in trade receivables — currently, the lion’s share of its assets.

“There is an urgent need for interim judicial managers to investigate the company’s affairs in the light of the prima facie pattern of fraudulent conduct on the part of the company’s management,” Tan wrote. “This is a case where a management timeout may actually serve to enhance and prevent the running down of the company’s assets and business.”

Radiant World has denied all wrongdoing. A spokesman did not immediately respond to requests for comment on Friday. Mizuho also did not immediately respond to Bloomberg queries. Mizuho’s lawyers from Shook Lin & Bok declined to comment.

A Bloomberg analysis of corporate records and visits to counterparties’ registered addresses had suggested that the vast majority was due from companies that said they owed Radiant nothing, firms closely related to Radiant itself, or obscure entities in the Middle East.

Tan pointed to over US$210 million in Radiant World said it was owed by Aspira Co Pte Ltd, Sapphire Minmetals Corporation Ltd and Quanterra International Ltd — companies which she noted were related to Radiant World itself, raising questions “as to how accurate or realisable these assets may be”.

The judge also rejected the company’s argument that a claim against Glencore plc for about US$2 billion should be regarded as a “realisable asset”. “It is pure speculation as to how the claim will fare and that it will be ‘resolved within 12 months’,” she wrote.

Glencore has said that the claim against it is “meritless”.

title: Goldman’s Moe says he’s in ‘stronger-for-longer camp’ on AI
article:
“We’re definitely in the stronger-for-longer camp,” Moe, Goldman’s chief Apac regional equity strategist, told Bloomberg TV’s Shery Ahn. He pointed to the estimated hyperscaler investment of around US$800 billion this year and about US$1.2 trillion in 2027 as the primary demand signal for Asia’s AI hardware supply chain.

Asia’s “exceedingly low” valuations also offer additional support, Moe said. The region trades at about 10 times earnings on a headline basis, at the cheaper end of historical ranges. Earnings growth will also provide a buffer against higher rates, he added.

For the rest of the year, Moe expects markets to remain “a bit bumpy” heading into the US midterm elections, with higher energy prices and geopolitical risk adding to the pressure. After that period, he said a rally towards the year-end is likely, driven by earnings growth and valuations.

title: Far East Orchard JV acquires London freehold site for 444-bed PBSA development
article:
Far East Orchard, through its joint venture company (JVCo), has acquired a freehold development site at 325 Borough High Street, Southwark, London, for GBP60 million ($102 million). The group intends to develop the site into a 444-bed purpose-built student accommodation (PBSA), targeted for completion by 2029.

Far East Orchard’s subsidiary, Borough High Street Development Limited and LDC (Portfolio) Limited entered into a sale and purchase agreement (SPA) on Sept 24.

Far East UK Student Accommodation Development Fund (FESAD), Far East Orchard’s UK PBSA development fund, holds an 85% interest in Borough High Street Development Limited through Far East PBSA Venture I Pte. Ltd. (FEPV).

The remaining interests are held equally by Far East Orchard Investments (UK) Pte Ltd (FEOIUK) and Aurum Investments (Private) Limited, with 7.5% stakes each. FEPV and FEOIUK are wholly-owned subsidiaries of Far East Orchard. Aurum Investments is wholly-owned by Woh Hup Holdings.

This is the group’s third acquisition and first development in London. The purchase will expand its portfolio across London, Manchester and Glasgow comprising 956 PBSA beds. The acquisition will also bring the group’s PBSA portfolio to over 60,000 beds owned and managed.

See also: Far East Orchard subsidiary in early talks for private fund to acquire London site, develop PBSA

“King’s Place marks a significant milestone for FESAD as our first development in London and the full deployment of the fund’s committed capital,” says Alan Tang, group CEO of Far East Orchard. “London remains one of the UK’s most attractive and supply-constrained student accommodation markets.”

“The acquisition will expand its development portfolio across three major UK cities. The development also demonstrates the strength of our integrated lodging platform, bringing together our investment, fund management, development, asset management and operating capabilities,” he adds.

See also: Centurion Corp acquires dormitory at Pasir Gudang for $67.2 mil

The site is located in London Zone 1 and is located close to several Russell Group universities including King’s College London, the London School of Economics and Political Science, Queen Mary University of London and Imperial College London. The site is also a four-minute walk from Borough Underground station and an eight-minute walk from Elephant & Castle station.

The development has received Gateway 2 approval, a milestone that allows construction to commence. Construction is targeted to begin in 4Q2026.
